sections.title: A suffix you've already half-met
sections.content: You've glimpsed -on/-en/-ön before without its name — hétfőn, szombaton for days of the week, a téren for "on the square". It's the superessive suffix, Hungarian's way of saying something rests ON a surface, as opposed to -ban/-ben, "inside" something. Now you'll use it freely, with any noun: back-vowel words take -on, front-unrounded words take -en, and front-rounded words take -ön.

items.english: We live on the second floor.
The key is on the book.

sections.content: The three-way split matches every other suffix with this shape you already know — the -ok/-ek/-ök verb endings work exactly the same way. If a word already ends in a vowel, you just add a bare -n instead: lépcső becomes lépcsőn, padló becomes padlón.
